body:
FOUND BY THE 2026-08-05 AUDIT (two-stores journey, CONFIRMED). Distinct from T103 (a SERVED store cannot pull — the capability); this is the REPORTING around the capability that exists.

1. `loam pull` against a down or mistyped peer prints exactly `loam: fetch failed`. No address, no cause (refused vs unresolvable vs TLS), no cure. The address the operator typed is right there; say it, and say what fetch saw.
2. NOTHING records the relationship: after a successful pull, no surface — health(), `loam store`, the peer list that does not exist — can answer "where does this store pull from, and when did it last succeed?" The operator's only record is shell history. A minimal durable answer (last-pull peer/time/count, surfaced in `loam store` and health) is the deliverable; the design question is where it lives (config? a delta? serving.json's sibling?) — recommend, do not decide silently.
3. The documented recipe dead-ends: README's federation section ends at a pull, and the next thing a real operator hits is `nothing is registered` (see T150 item 4 for the door's message; this item is the DOCS side — carry the recipe through registration to a served read-back).

RAILS: pull-failure message test (down peer, wrong host — assert address + cure in the message); a record test (pull, then read the relationship back from the chosen surface); README recipe executed end-to-end by the docs test pattern if one exists, else a script.

WHO MERGES: item 2 adds a surface — Myk. Items 1 and 3 are report/docs repairs on the ordinary bar.
title: Federation cannot say what happened: a bare fetch failed, no record of the relationship, and a docs path that dead-ends
